theme_central: Protecting oneself from life's great trials (fitan) through faith, divine knowledge, and reliance on Allah — hence its recommended recitation every Friday (protection against the Dajjal).
sources_note: The "4 trials" structure: a broad, well-documented consensus (surahsofquran.com, jfln.org, onepathnetwork.com, backtojannah.com).

branches.title: Opening
branches.resume: Praise of Allah for a Book "without crookedness" — its mission: to warn and to give good news.

children.t: The Book revealed without deviation, to warn of a severe punishment
Good news for the believers, warning against excessive grief
This world is a fleeting ornament, a means of testing

branches.title: The Trial of Faith — The People of the Cave
branches.resume: Young believers flee persecution, a miraculous sleep of ~300 years.

children.t: Young believers flee a hostile society
The sleep in the cave, divine protection
The awakening, a debate over their number and the exact duration

branches.title: The Trial of Wealth — The Two Gardens
branches.resume: A rich, arrogant man looks down on his more modest believing neighbour.

children.t: The pride of the owner of the two gardens
The warning of his believing companion
Ruin of the garden — wealth is fleeting

branches.title: The Trial of Knowledge — Musa and Khidr
branches.resume: Musa seeks a servant who holds hidden divine knowledge; accepting the limits of one's own knowledge.

children.t: Musa sets out in search of the knowledgeable servant
Three incomprehensible acts by Khidr, the condition of patience broken
Explanation: the hidden meaning behind each act

branches.title: The Trial of Power — Dhul-Qarnayn
branches.resume: A just and powerful king; he builds the barrier against Gog and Magog.

children.t: Journey to the west and the east, justice toward the peoples
Building the barrier — power in the service of justice

branches.title: Closing
branches.resume: Reminder of the Last Judgment — Allah's word is infinite.

children.t: Destruction of the barrier, a sign of the end times
The vain deeds of those who doubted meeting Allah
The ink of the sea would not be enough to write Allah's words
